# GitPersona v0.1.0 — The right Git account in every folder

Released on `2026-10-24`.

> GitPersona gives each directory its own Git identity: commits, pushes, `gh` and `glab` use the account that
> belongs to the folder you are in, in every tool that runs Git, and `gitpersona verify` proves no repository uses
> the wrong one.

## Summary

This is the first public release of GitPersona. Bind your folders to a profile once, and every repository inside
commits, pushes and opens pull requests as the right account — in the terminal, in your IDE and in GUI Git clients —
with nothing to switch when you change projects. It runs on macOS (Apple silicon and Intel) and Linux (x86_64 and
arm64).

## Who this release is for

You keep more than one Git account on one machine — a personal GitHub account and a work one, a client's GitLab
server, a second account for open source — and you have committed with the wrong email or pushed as the wrong user at
least once.

If you have ever:

- noticed a work commit signed with your personal email, after it was pushed
- run `gh auth switch` before a pull request, and forgotten to switch back
- kept a `~/.gitconfig` full of `includeIf` rules you no longer dare to touch
- cloned a repository and found it pushed as whichever account the keychain remembered

then GitPersona replaces all of that with one rule per folder, and a check that tells you whether it holds.

## What you can do now

**Set everything up in one step.** Run `gitpersona setup --web`: it finds the accounts you are signed in to with
`gh`, your existing `includeIf` identities, your SSH aliases and your repositories, and shows one complete proposal.
Nothing is written until you click Apply, and every file is backed up first.

**Stop thinking about accounts.** `cd` into a project and use `git`, `gh`, `glab`, your IDE or a GUI client as
usual. Commits get the folder's author and email; pushes use the folder's token or SSH key; `gh pr create` opens
the pull request as the folder's account.

**Prove it.** `gitpersona verify` lists, for every repository, the author its commits use and the account each
remote pushes as, and flags anything that would use another identity — with the exact command to fix it.

**See it all on one page.** `gitpersona ui` opens a local console in English or Chinese: accounts with their
folders, every repository's check, a diff of each change before it is applied, health checks, shells and backups.

**Undo anything.** Every change is backed up; `gitpersona rollback` restores any of them, and `gitpersona uninstall`
puts your Git configuration back as it was.

## What's new

### Identities that follow your folders

- **One folder, one identity.** Bind folders to a profile; every repository inside follows it. A pin handles the odd
  repository that lives elsewhere, and the most specific rule wins. It uses Git's own `includeIf`, so there is no
  wrapper around `git` and nothing to remember.
- **One rule for everything:** commit author and email, HTTPS credentials, SSH key, commit signing, and the `gh` /
  `glab` account.
- **Several accounts per host.** Two GitHub accounts, three GitLab accounts on a company server: each folder pushes
  with its own account's token. GitHub tokens are borrowed from `gh`; other hosts use your own credential store.

### Setup

- `gitpersona setup` (terminal) and `setup --web` (browser) propose a complete configuration from what you already
  have: one profile per signed-in account with its public name and email, your existing identities and SSH aliases,
  folders from your repositories' remotes, and pins for repositories that differ from their folder.
- Your own `includeIf` rules keep working outside the folders you give to profiles. Setup never removes a rule that
  does more than a profile can.

### Checking repositories

- `gitpersona verify` checks the commit author and the push account of every repository in your profiles' folders
  and pins, and flags local overrides, tokens written in remote URLs and SSH connections shared between keys. It
  reads only settings; `--ssh` asks each SSH host which account a key really signs in as.
- `gitpersona doctor` checks the whole setup, from the Git version to each account's `gh` sign-in, and explains how
  to fix each problem; `--fix` repairs what it safely can.

### Web console

- `gitpersona ui`: an overview with what needs attention, accounts with their identities, folders and pins, the
  repository check, a diff preview before applying, health checks, shells and backups.
- English and Simplified Chinese: it follows your system's language, then your browser's; switch it in the sidebar.
  Light and dark themes, and it works on a phone-sized screen.

### Shells

- fish, zsh and bash: your prompt can show the account Git uses here, and `gh` / `glab` follow the folder you are in.

## Privacy and security

- **Never stores tokens.** GitHub tokens stay in `gh`; other hosts' tokens stay in your system keychain or Git
  Credential Manager. GitPersona keeps no copy and never prints them.
- **Never reads your keys.** Private key files are only checked to exist; ssh uses them, GitPersona never opens them.
- **Local only.** The web console listens only on 127.0.0.1, behind a link that works once, and stops after 15
  minutes without use. There is no telemetry.
- **Only when you ask.** It connects to the network only to read your accounts' public names and emails during
  setup, and to the SSH hosts when you run `check-ssh` or `verify --ssh`.

## Install

- Script (macOS and Linux, fully automatic): `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/weikxs/gitpersona/main/install.sh | sh`
- Homebrew (macOS and Linux): `brew install weikxs/tap/gitpersona`
- Go 1.26+: `go install github.com/weikxs/gitpersona/cmd/gitpersona@v0.1.0`
- A package or archive below; check it against `checksums.txt`

| File | Platform |
|---|---|
| `gitpersona_0.1.0_darwin_arm64.tar.gz` | macOS, Apple silicon |
| `gitpersona_0.1.0_darwin_amd64.tar.gz` | macOS, Intel |
| `gitpersona_0.1.0_linux_amd64.deb` / `_arm64.deb` | Debian, Ubuntu (x86_64 / arm64) |
| `gitpersona_0.1.0_linux_amd64.rpm` / `_arm64.rpm` | Fedora, RHEL (x86_64 / arm64) |
| `gitpersona_0.1.0_linux_amd64.apk` / `_arm64.apk` | Alpine (x86_64 / arm64) |
| `gitpersona_0.1.0_linux_amd64.pkg.tar.zst` / `_arm64.pkg.tar.zst` | Arch (x86_64 / arm64) |
| `gitpersona_0.1.0_linux_amd64.tar.gz` / `_arm64.tar.gz` | Any Linux (x86_64 / arm64) |

Then sign in to each GitHub account once with `gh auth login`, and run `gitpersona setup --web`.

## Compatibility

- macOS 12 or newer on Apple silicon and Intel; Linux on x86_64 and arm64 (glibc or musl: Debian, Ubuntu, Fedora,
  Arch, Alpine and others). Windows is planned.
- Git 2.31 or newer (2.36 or newer if you have your own `includeIf "hasconfig:…"` rules).
- For GitHub profiles, the GitHub CLI 2.40 or newer; for other hosts, a credential helper such as the system keychain
  or Git Credential Manager.
- The web console is in English and Simplified Chinese; the command line is in English.

## What's coming next

- Windows support.

## Notes

- The macOS binary is not signed or notarized by Apple; Homebrew and the install script remove the quarantine flag.
  By hand: **Open Anyway** in System Settings → Privacy & Security. See
  [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/weikxs/gitpersona/blob/main/SECURITY.md#release-binaries-and-macos).
